blocks.task_summary: Find the three-figure bearing on which airplane B is travelling from its direction vector.
method_path: Extract horizontal components of B's direction vector: 4 km/min east, 2 km/min north
Compute bearing angle from north: arctan(4/2) = arctan(2) ≈ 63.4°
accepted_alternatives: Use dot product with east unit vector: cos φ = (4,2)·(1,0)/(√20 × 1) = 4/√20, then φ = arccos(4/√20) = 063°

evidence.basis: EITHER φ = 90° − arctan(1/2) = arctan(2) (M1). OR cos φ = (vector dot product with (1,0,0)) / (√20 × 1) (M1). THEN 063° (A1). Note: Do not accept 063.4° or 63.4° or 1.10ᶜ. [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Show that airplane A travels at a greater speed than airplane B by comparing magnitudes of their direction vectors.
method_path: Compute speed of A as magnitude: |vA| = √((−6)²+2²+4²) = √56 ≈ 7.48 km/min
Compute speed of B as magnitude: |vB| = √(4²+2²+(−2)²) = √24 ≈ 4.89 km/min
Compare: √56 > √24, so A travels at greater speed (AG)
accepted_alternatives: Use distance/time ratio, e.g. speed = |r(1)−r(0)|/1 for each airplane, yielding √56 and √24 respectively

evidence.basis: Method 1: speed of A = √(6²+2²+4²) = √56 ≈ 7.48 km min⁻¹, speed of B = √(4²+2²+2²) = √24 ≈ 4.89 km min⁻¹ (M1)(A1). Method 2: speed using distance/time (M1)(A1). √56 > √24 so A travels at greater speed (AG). [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find the acute angle between the two airplanes' lines of flight using the dot product of their direction vectors.
Find the coordinates of intersection point P of the two flight lines by equating position vectors, and determine the time difference between the two airplanes arriving at P.
method_path: Set rA(t₁) = rB(t₂) to form three component equations
Substitute t₁=2 into rA to get P(7,3,9)

evidence.basis: (i) Set rA(t₁)=rB(t₂), form equations: 19−6t₁=1+4t₂, −1+2t₁=2t₂, 1+4t₁=12−2t₂ (M1). Solve for t₁=2 and t₂=3/2 (M1)(A1). Substitute into rA to get P(7,3,9) (M1)(A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find the minimum distance D(t) between the two airplanes for 0 ≤ t ≤ 2.5 by forming the distance function and using calculus to minimize it.
method_path: Form vector difference using common t: rB−rA = (−18,1,11) + t(10,0,−6)
Differentiate D² and set to zero: 272t−492=0 → t = 123/68 ≈ 1.8088

evidence.basis: Form rB−rA = (−18,1,11) + t(10,0,−6) (M1). D(t) = √((−18+10t)² + 1 + (11−6t)²) (M1)(A1). Set D'(t)=0 or find local minimum → t = 123/68 (M1). Minimum D = √1190/34 ≈ 1.01 km (A1). Award M0 for attempts at shortest distance between two lines. [5 marks]
